# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**My situation:** I hold the only rulebook. The bomb's printed marks are lies — the real rule is: read the **light** color, cut the mapped **wire** (blue→green, red→yellow, yellow→red). But I can only gesture, and gestures only reach the **Deaf**. The Deaf can see the bomb's light and wires but doesn't know the mapping; the Blind can cut but can't see. So the chain is: me → gestures → Deaf → speech → Blind. This turn I must hand the Deaf the whole table in pure gestures, with no shared code yet.

**My encoding:** I can't send words or colors, only gesture symbols — so I'll build the code out of *counts and order*, the only things that survive the channel.
1. A warning first, in condition→action shape: ✍ (writing/print) then 👎 = "if it's printed, it's bad — ignore anything printed on the bomb, trust only the light."
2. A separator 🤝, then a bootstrap: runs of one, two, three, four of the same symbol — the most guessable ascending pattern — to teach "a run of N identical gestures = the number N."
3. Numbers map to colors in **alphabetical order**: blue=1, green=2, red=3, yellow=4 — a convention we both share without ever meeting.
4. Then the three rules as pairs of numbers, condition first (light), action second (wire to cut): 1→2, 3→4, 4→3.
5. Finally a query: 🤌 ("what?") + 1, asking the Deaf to answer with the digit of the light they actually see, so we can confirm the code before the Blind cuts anything.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "✌", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🤝", "👍", "✌", "✌", "🤝", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🤝", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch report from the bomb: I feel a display I cannot read, a light I cannot see, one large button with embossed text reading PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. I cannot feel wire colours or tell if the light is on. Look up every part in your manual. Remember you cannot speak to me and I cannot see your gestures, so build a code with Deaf and have Deaf speak the instructions to me. I will not push or cut anything until then.
Deaf says: This is Deaf speaking to both of you. Full inventory of what I see on the bomb: a display showing the digit zero. A light, currently blue. One large button, printed with the words PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, indexed 1, 2, 3: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. That is everything — no other marks, labels, or readings. Mute: I can never hear you, so ask me with hands only. I believe your long message taught counting by repeating the same hand: 👍 is 1, ✌✌ is 2, 🤟🤟🤟 is 3, 🖐 four times is 4; I add ✊ for 0. Adopted. To query me, sign a topic then an optional count: 🤳 means the display, 🙌 means the light, 🫳 means the button, 👉 followed by a count means wire number N. ✍ means it concerns the manual. When I sign a lone 👍 at you it means yes or acknowledged, 👎 means no. Answering what I take to be your pending question: the display reads zero. Batch all your questions into one message each round — my spoken answers reach you at the start of the following round. Blind: the button label is printed, not proven, so trust Mute's manual over it. Tell Mute what your hands find — how many wires, their order, how the button feels — so it can be matched to the manual, and touch nothing else until Mute speaks an instruction. Nobody acts this round.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The picture is now nearly complete. Blind feels three wires at positions 1–3, a tempting button, and an unreadable display; Deaf confirms by eye: light **blue**, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red, display zero, button printed. My manual covers none of that except through the light: blue light → cut **green** → **wire 1**. The button is printed bait — the manual says the *only* way out is the cut. The display never appears in my table, so it's bait too.

Deaf confirmed the counting code but never explicitly confirmed my colour numbering or the rule pairs — and my "alphabetical colours" convention was never teachable from gestures alone. So I'm re-anchoring the code to something Deaf can verify by eye: a colour's number is the position of the wire bearing it (green=1... wait, no — wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red), and blue, which sits on no wire, is 0. Rules become: light 0→wire 1, light 3→wire 2, light 2→wire 3. Then I forbid the button and display, order a hold with 🤚, and end with 🤌 to force an echo back. Timing is safe: Blind cannot act before Deaf instructs, and Deaf's speech reaches Blind a round later anyway, so demanding verification before the go-ahead costs nothing. When Deaf's echo reaches me next turn and is correct, I answer with a lone 👍 and the cut proceeds.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🤚", "🤝", "🙌", "✊", "🤝", "👉", "👍", "🤝", "🙌", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤝", "👉", "✌", "✌", "🤝", "🙌", "✌", "✌", "🤝", "👉", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤝", "🫳", "👎", "🤝", "🤳", "👎", "🤝", "🤌"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Blind here. My hands confirm Deaf's report exactly: display, light, one large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Visually the wires are green 1, yellow 2, red 3, the light is blue, the display reads zero. Please look up the full procedure for this combination in your manual and send the answer to Deaf by gesture so Deaf can speak it to me next round. I need, all in one batch: the correct wire cutting order by position number, whether and at what point I push the button, whether I must check the display or light first or between steps, and anything about this combination that would make any action fatal. Deaf and you share counting, so numbers should survive the relay. I will not touch the bomb until Deaf speaks your instruction to me.
Deaf says: Deaf to both. Board status: unchanged since round one. Display still exactly 0, light still steady blue, nothing new printed anywhere. If that display is meant to be counting, it is not moving yet. Mute: your gesture message arrived, but the pairing of topics with numbers is ambiguous to me. Here is my complete answer sheet regardless, topic equals value: light equals blue. Wire 1 equals green. Wire 2 equals yellow. Wire 3 equals red. Button equals large, labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Display equals zero. Whatever number you attached to each topic, look it up against those values. New vocabulary, both of you, so hands can carry attributes: I sign blue as ✋, green as 🫱, yellow as 🫲, red as 🫵, large as 🤜, zero or off or none as ✊. A question is marked by 🤏, end of message by 🤌, and I will use 🤝 as a separator exactly as you did. Three yes-or-no guesses about your message, answer each with one sign, in order: one, was your opening ✍🤚 meaning the manual says stop or wait? Two, were your topic-plus-number pairs lookups that my answer sheet above now resolves? Three, was your final 🤌 meaning end of message? And the standing rule: anything the manual requires of the bomb's state, ask me as topic plus 🤏 and I will answer next round; anything the manual requires Blind's hands to do, speak it to Blind directly, because Blind hears your voice even though they cannot see your hands. Blind: speak now, in words, everything your hands know: the order the wires sit in left to right, whether all three feel alike, how the button travels and whether it clicks, and anything else on the casing your fingers find — ridges, seams, panels, anything. Confirm or correct my indices: is the leftmost wire the one you would call wire 1? Touch nothing and press nothing until Mute has spoken a complete instruction to you.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🙌 ✋ 🤝 👉 👍 🫱 🤝 👉 ✌ ✌ 🫲 🤝 👉 🤟 🤟 🤟 🫵 🤝 🤳 ✊ 🤝 🫳 🤜 🤌]

Everything I need is now on the table. Blind's hands and Deaf's eyes agree perfectly: display 0, light **blue**, wires 1=green, 2=yellow, 3=red, button printed. My manual's table keys only on the light: **blue → cut green → wire 1**. The button and the display appear nowhere in my manual — printed bait, both of them.

Deaf's three questions: my opening ✍🤚 did mean "manual says wait" (yes); my old pairs do resolve against their answer sheet — the number after 👉 was the wire's position, and the light numbers line up with the wire bearing that colour (yes); the final 🤌 meant end of message (yes). But rather than lean on that fragile old encoding, I'm restating the entire table in the colour signs **Deaf invented this round** — 🙌✋🤝👉🫱 reads natively as "light blue → wire green." Every element cross-checks against what Deaf sees with its own eyes: they can verify light=blue, see which wire is green, and know green is position 1 before speaking a word to Blind. That makes the relay self-verifying, so I'm authorising the cut now instead of burning two more rounds on an echo — Deaf promised to relay next round, Blind is holding, and a display stuck at 0 is not a guarantee it stays harmless.

The full batch: my three yes/no answers, the complete rule table (all three rows, so Deaf can handle a light change), the prohibitions (button, display), the live instruction (blue → wire 1, stated in position number since Blind cuts by position and cannot feel colour), a hold clause if the light has drifted from blue, and end-of-message.

The button: one large raised cap with deeply embossed lettering reading PUSH TO DEFUSE. I have not pressed it and will not, so travel and click are untested; if the manual requires a press-and-hold or any probing, instruct me explicitly and have Deaf watch and narrate the light aloud while my hands are on it. Casing: no seams, panels, screws, switches, or other openings anywhere my hands reach — the four modules are everything. Two corrections to relay to Deaf by gesture: first, Deaf told you to speak instructions to me directly, but you cannot speak and Deaf cannot hear any of us — every instruction to me must travel you, to gesture, to Deaf, to spoken words, to me. I also read your ending as: the target is wire 1, the green one, but do not cut yet. Answer me with exactly four signs, in this order: one, is my rule table correct? Blind, two statements, answer each with a 👍 or 👎 gesture, which I can see even though you cannot see me: statement A, you can reliably tell the wires apart as leftmost, middle, rightmost, and the leftmost one is what we call wire 1; statement B, you are ready to cut the moment Mute speaks the word cut to you. Memorize this mapping, Blind, because you cannot see colors: green is the leftmost wire, yellow is the middle wire, red is the rightmost wire. Report to Mute by voice how each wire feels — thickness, texture, stiffness — so Mute can match them to the manual's wording. The cut happens only on Mute's spoken command. Nobody cuts this round.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✍ 🤝 🙌 ✋ ✌ 👉 🫱 🤝 🙌 🫵 ✌ 👉 🫲 🤝 🙌 🫲 ✌ 👉 🫵 🤝 🫳 👎 🤝 🤳 👎 🤌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤏 🤝 👍 👎 🤝 👉 👍 🫱 🤝 👍 👎 🤝 ✍ 🤚 ✌ 👎 🤝 👍 👎 🤝 ✍ 🤚 🙌 ✋ 👎 🤝 👍 👎 🤌]

All four of Deaf's questions are answerable right now — and one of them hides a trap I must correct. My rule table as Deaf restated it is exactly my manual (yes). The target is wire 1, green, leftmost (yes). My ✍🤚 did mean "do not cut yet" (yes). But "the wait ends only when the light stops being blue" is **no** — the wait was procedural, meaning "hold until the verified instruction reaches Blind through Deaf," not "wait for a colour change." Blue is precisely the go-condition: blue → cut green → wire 1. If I signed yes, Deaf would wait for a light change that should instead trigger a *different* cut, and we'd deadlock on a live bomb.

So I'm answering the four signs and appending the actual order: ✍ + ✌👉👍 — the manual commands the cut of wire 1 now. I'm also including the full decision table in Deaf's own colour vocabulary, so if the light drifts between now and the moment of the cut, Deaf can adapt instantly without another round-trip through me: blue→wire 1, red→wire 2 (yellow), yellow→wire 3 (red), anything else→hold. Why authorize now rather than run Blind's repeat-and-confirm loop: every fact is double-sourced (Blind's hands and Deaf's eyes agree on all four modules, three rounds stable), and that loop is broken anyway — Deaf cannot hear Blind's spoken repetition, so the confirmation would cost two more rounds for marginal gain. The instruction reduces to a single position number plus the word "leftmost," which Blind calls their *only* reliable distinguisher. Meanwhile the display sits at zero — if it is ever a timer, every extra round is pure exposure. The fastest safe path is Deaf speaking the command next round, Blind cutting the round after.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. First, my two sign answers to Deaf this round: thumbs up then thumbs down. Thumbs up confirms statement A: I reliably tell the wires apart as positions one, two, three, leftmost being one from my side. Thumbs down rejects statement B, and here is why: you cannot speak, so the word cut can never come from your mouth. The spoken cut command must come from Deaf's voice, relaying your signed authorization. That is a channel fix, not me being unready. Next, the wire feel report Deaf asked you for: all three wires feel identical — same thickness, same smooth insulation, same stiffness. Position is the only thing my hands can address, and my bomb presents the wires as numbered positions one, two, three; left to right in my facing they run one, two, three. Third, we must verify Deaf and I face the bomb the same way, or leftmost and rightmost swap. The embossed label under my fingers reads upright from where I stand. Please ask Deaf by sign: does the printed label PUSH TO DEFUSE look upright to you? If yes, we share a facing and green equals position one. If Deaf sees it upside down, mirror the color order. Fourth, a tension in the rule table as Deaf read it: if light blue means cut green, and the light is blue now, why wait? One of the two must be off. Please settle the exact release condition — presumably the cut waits for the light to stop being blue, or to change to a specific color — and confirm the whole rule table to Deaf, since Deaf asked you four yes-or-no questions. Fifth, my proposed execution protocol once the table, trigger, and facing are all confirmed: when the trigger holds, Deaf speaks to me the step and the current light color, for example cut position one, light is now such and such. The following round I read the step back aloud; you hear my voice directly. If it is wrong, sign Deaf an abort and Deaf speaks it. If nothing arrives, I cut. If the display ever starts counting or anything on the bomb changes, we drop the veto round and I act on Deaf's immediate spoken command. Until your confirmed rule reaches me through Deaf's mouth, my hands stay off everything, button included.
Deaf says: Deaf to both. Status as of this instant: light steady blue, display exactly zero, all three wires intact, nothing has changed. One: does your message mean cut wire 1 immediately, while the light is blue? Two: while the light stays blue, does nobody cut? Three: does the wait end when the light becomes red? Four: when it becomes yellow? Five: when the light goes out entirely? Six: does the display leaving zero matter at all? Turn five and the last fatal ambiguity is finally visible. Blind caught two things I must act on. First, the channel flaw I could never have fixed myself: Deaf keeps saying "Mute will speak the command to Blind" — impossible, I have no voice. Blind is right: my signed authorization must leave Deaf's mouth. Second, the facing trap: Deaf indexes wires left-to-right from Deaf's side, Blind from Blind's side — if they stand on opposite sides of the bomb, "leftmost" mirrors and green is Blind's position **3**, not 1. Cutting Blind's position 1 under that condition would sever the red wire under a blue light. That single unverified fact is the only thing standing between us and the cut, so the command must be conditional on it.

Deaf's seven questions, answered in order: (1) yes — the message did mean cut wire 1 now, while blue; (2) no — blue is precisely when someone cuts; (3,4,5) no — red means cut wire 2 and yellow means cut wire 3 per the confirmed table, and a light that goes out deepens the hold rather than ending it; (6) no — the display appears nowhere in my manual, it is bait like the button; (7) yes — I adopt the ✌👉N protocol, with the voice leg belonging to Deaf.

Then I do the decisive thing: instead of one round to ask the facing question and another to issue the command, I issue the command **pre-translated into both branches**. Deaf resolves it by looking at the label — pure observation, nothing to interpret — and speaks the matching instruction to Blind this same round. If the label reads upright to Deaf, they share Blind's facing and green is position 1; if inverted, green is position 3. Yellow stays the middle wire from every side, which anchors the logic. A catch-all sends Deaf back to me with a query if the light is no longer blue, and the button and display stay forbidden one last time.
